messages:
julia: FYI forwarded a customer ticket — acme reported a 3x p99 spike and a handful of 502s starting ~09:10 UTC. They say requests that normally hit eu-west are routing to us-west instead. attaching their trace id: trace-0af3b9
kevin: can you paste the customer's original headers + request-id? need to correlate with our traces.
marta: grabbing traces now. I see lots of requests with client_region=eu-west-1 but egress_region=us-west-2 in the sample span. looks like a mismatch at the edge->egress hop. :thinking_face:
julia: customer pasted this header set: `x-rdw-client-region: eu-west-1`, `x-rdw-request-id: acme-2026-03-17-09:09:22`, `host: api.redwood.ai`. they also included curl repro: `curl -v -H \"Authorization: Bearer <token>\" -H \"x-rdw-client-region: eu-west-1\" https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate`
kevin: ok repro command, thanks. running an internal cURL to reproduce.
infra-bot: [automated trace created] tracebot-id=tb-2475001111 span_count=18 top_hop=proxy-edge-03 next_hop=regional-egress-11 lat_ms=2400
tracebot: Quick summary: 70% of traces in that window show proxy-edge-03 routing to regional-egress-usw instead of regional-egress-euw. Healthcheck failures on regional-egress-euw observed at 09:08:41 UTC.
marta: looking at healthcheck logs: egress-euw returned 503 for the control-plane health probe due to a stale cert rotation task hitting a slow disk. it flipped Unhealthy and the router removed the pool. but the regional routing rules should prefer other eu nodes, not bounce to us-west. investigating why affinity didn't pick other eu egresses.
kevin: possible bug in region-affinity selector when pool size=1 and `allow_cross_region` fallback toggle is true. can we check the canary rollout we pushed last night? the new selector change might have the logic to fallback to any available region if local pool unhealthy.
marta: confirmed: canary `egress-routing-v2` enabled on 20% of requests for that customer org. it contains a codepath that considers candidate pools by latency score but didn't require region match unless strict_affinity flag present. not good.
ops-oncall: timeline: 09:07 deploy canary, 09:08 egress-euw healthcheck fail, 09:09 customer spike + 502s. rolling back canary now.
kevin: while rollback goes, quick mitigation for acme: they can set header `x-redwood-region: eu-west-1` to force region pin. share that with support as a temporary workaround. also gating toggle `allow_cross_region` to false org-wide will prevent fallback while we fix.
julia: passing workaround to customer now. they asked for repro steps we used. I sent the curl with `-H \"x-redwood-region: eu-west-1\"` and asked them to try.
infra-bot: rollback of canary `egress-routing-v2` completed at 09:16 UTC. traffic back to stable routing. healthchecks for regional-egress-euw recovered at 09:17:10 UTC.
kevin: root cause summary for ticket: canary introduced permissive fallback behavior that allowed cross-region egress when local pool unhealthy. combined with a transient healthcheck failure on the only eu egress node serving that cluster, requests fell back to us-west causing increased latency and some 502s.
marta: remediation: 1) revert permissive fallback in canary (done), 2) add strict_affinity opt-in flag defaulting to true for orgs with region affinity, 3) add guardrail so fallback to another continent requires an explicit override, 4) improve healthcheck snafu detection + alerting. I'll open a follow-up infra PR.
ops-oncall: recommend adding a short KB entry in Support on this pattern (canary + single-node pool => cross-region bounce) and a quick script to set `x-redwood-region` for customers while we remediate.
julia: thanks team — I'll update the support ticket with the root cause and the temporary workaround. please ping me when PR is merged so I can notify customer of permanent fix ETA. :thumbsup:
